answer: A staking bond works like a dune that only holds its shape when every grain pays to stay: an agent must lock collateral before it can transact, and misbehavior burns part of that bond. Honest agents see the horizon of future earnings outweigh the one-time gain of a fake identity, while a Sybil attacker must fund a whole mesa of separate bonds, so the cost of forging identities scales linearly with the attack instead of being nearly free.
